theorem: For n centered observations x_1, ..., x_n in R^d (centered meaning sum_i x_i = 0, i.e. the sample mean has been subtracted), the sample covariance matrix S = (1/(n-1)) * sum_{i=1}^n x_i x_i^T has rank at most min(d, n-1).
proof: Let X be the d x n matrix whose columns are the centered observations x_1, ..., x_n. Then S = (1/(n-1)) X X^T. Step 1 (column-space bound): rank(S) = rank(X X^T) = rank(X), because for any matrix X, the null space of X X^T equals the null space of X^T (if X X^T v = 0 then v^T X X^T v = ||X^T v||^2 = 0, so X^T v = 0), and X X^T and X therefore share the same rank; equivalently, the column space of X X^T is the span of the columns of X. Hence rank(S) = rank(X) <= min(d, n), giving the generic bound min(d, n). Step 2 (centering removes one degree of freedom): centering imposes the linear constraint sum_i x_i = 0, i.e. X * 1_n = 0 where 1_n is the all-ones vector. So the n columns of X lie in the (n-1)-dimensional subspace of coefficient vectors orthogonal to 1_n; concretely, any one column is a linear combination of the other n-1 (x_n = -sum_{i<n} x_i), so the column rank of X is at most n-1. Step 3 (combine): rank(S) = rank(X) <= min(d, n-1), as claimed. Sharpness: the bound is attained whenever the centered points span a min(d, n-1)-dimensional subspace (generic position), so 'at most' cannot be improved without extra hypotheses. QED.
consequence: In a 42-group MLIP error-geometry audit where each group contributes only n=3 materials observed in d=3 elastic-constant space, every per-group sample covariance matrix has rank at most min(3, 3-1) = 2, regardless of the data. The 3x3 covariance matrix is therefore forced to be singular: its third eigenvalue lambda_3 is identically zero (up to floating-point roundoff) for every one of the 42 groups, and at most two eigenvalues can be positive. The eigenspectrum (lambda_1 >= lambda_2 >= lambda_3 = 0) is structurally degenerate, not empirically informative. Consequently, a monotonicity test on the sorted eigenvalues — e.g. checking lambda_1 >= lambda_2 >= lambda_3 across groups, or checking that the spectrum decays — is tautological: sorting enforces lambda_1 >= lambda_2 >= lambda_3 by construction, and rank <= 2 forces lambda_3 = 0 by linear algebra, so the 'test' passes for every group no matter what the underlying MLIP errors look like. It carries zero statistical power and can never falsify any hypothesis about error geometry; it is a property of the sampling design (n=3 points in d=3 space), not of the model.
valid_test: A valid test would require sampling variation beyond the rank constraint — either more materials per group (n > d, so the covariance can be full-rank and the eigenvalues become genuine random variables) or a hypothesis about an estimable quantity (e.g. the direction of the top eigenvector, the ratio lambda_1/lambda_2 conditioned on n-1 degrees of freedom, or cross-group comparisons against a pooled/null distribution obtained by permutation or bootstrap) rather than a deterministic consequence of sorting and rank deficiency.
